pass_1.finding: The 2012 guide names N701–N712 for the 96-sample Index Kit and N701–N706 for the 24-sample kit; Index 1 i7 is eight bases adjacent to P7, and table lists N701 TAAGGCGA through N712 GTAGAGGA. pass_2.locations: Original Illumina Nextera XT Sample Preparation Guide 15031942 Rev C October 2012 text lines 48–60, 380–395, 455–475, 1195–1248, 2165–2285; original SCRB supplement 003236-1.pdf.txt lines 58–74; ran scrape_primers on complete SCRB source bundle and checked guide/source hits.
pass_2.finding: Independently confirmed the original 2012 guide provides N701–N712 i7 index inventory and exact eight-base values adjacent to P7, with six-index 24-sample and twelve-index 96-sample kits. SCRB replaces only the i5 primer with P5NEXTPT5 and leaves the i7 primer/member generic in its Methods and Fig. S1. The guide establishes a contemporary candidate family but neither identifies the SCRB-selected N7xx well nor proves the exact kit lot/revision used.

missing_claims.evidence: 003236-1.pdf.txt Table S2, extracted lines 1496 onward, prints two 384-well sets; Methods lines 43–46 distinguish D1/D2 from D3. The table set-1 heading is duplicated “D2 and D2”; page discloses this source discrepancy and model uses a six-base placeholder.

missing_claims.claim: Specific Nextera N7xx well/index used by the original SCRB-seq experiments and exact 2014 kit-lot primer identity
missing_claims.evidence: SCRB Supplementary Methods lines 63–70 replace the i5 primer and Fig. S1 lines 276–289 show generic [i7]. Current official sequence table lines 181–205 and original 2012 Illumina guide lines 2173–2274 define family architecture and N701–N712 candidates, but neither chooses the SCRB experiment well. Two independent readers checked the 2012 guide; neither it nor SCRB identifies the selected well.

conclusion: Original SCRB preprint, supplements, current official Nextera sequence table and recovered 2012 Illumina guide have two independent located reads. Table S2 publishes both six-base well-barcode sets; the guide lists N701–N712 i7 candidates. No original source selects the experiment-specific N7xx well or proves the 2014 kit lot/revision, so that narrow claim remains blocked.
